name: Fire Watch
objective: Map wildfires and the health of forests from orbit.
description: Your first mission stays close to home. Low Earth Orbit is easy to reach and easy to talk to, but the spacecraft spends about a third of every orbit in Earth's shadow.
fact: Satellites in Low Earth Orbit circle the planet about 15 times a day, so they pass through Earth's shadow 15 times a day too.

name: Moon Mapper
objective: Map the Moon's surface and search for water ice in dark polar craters.
description: The Moon is 384,000 km away. You need fuel to brake into orbit, and your radio signal is weaker than at Earth.
fact: Radio signals take about 1.3 seconds to travel from the Moon to Earth.

name: Red Planet Weather
objective: Study the Martian atmosphere and track giant dust storms.
description: Mars is 1.5 times farther from the Sun than Earth, so solar panels make less than half the power. Messages take minutes to arrive.
fact: Depending on where Earth and Mars are in their orbits, a radio message takes between 3 and 22 minutes to cross the gap.

name: Giant's Secret
objective: Look inside Jupiter: its deep atmosphere, its core and its powerful magnetic field.
description: At 5.2 AU, sunlight is only 4% as strong as at Earth, and Jupiter's radiation belts destroy unprotected electronics.
fact: Juno was the first spacecraft to fly to Jupiter on solar power alone. Its three solar wings are each about 9 meters long.

name: Ringworld
objective: Study Saturn's rings and the icy plumes of its moon Enceladus.
description: At 9.5 AU, sunlight is about 90 times weaker than at Earth. Solar panels are nearly useless here.
fact: Cassini studied Saturn for 13 years, powered by nuclear RTGs instead of solar panels.
